issues.description: ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel has inconsistent types between the specification and the reference solution: the UML in the problem statement declares excellencyLevel as double, but the solution implements the field as int and also uses int in the constructor parameter and getter return type. This makes the expected constructor signature/field type unclear for students and can lead to failing tests if they follow the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the UML by changing ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel to double and updating the constructor parameter and getter return type to double (or, if int is intended, update the UML/problem statement to specify int consistently).
